implementation_notes: C has no synchronized methods and no standard concurrency classes, so the balking object is a struct that owns its state and a pthread_mutex_t: the guarded method takes the mutex with pthread_mutex_trylock(), which returns EBUSY immediately instead of waiting, then checks the state inside the same critical section. The classic structure - predicate, early return, one transition - is therefore written out in full, and only the non-blocking acquisition comes from the platform. When callers must wait for the state to become permissible, replace trylock with pthread_mutex_lock plus a condition variable (Guarded Suspension); a plain int state read without the mutex is a data race.
pitfalls: pthread_mutex_trylock reports contention as EBUSY, so 'lock busy' and 'state forbids it' collapse into the same return value - report a distinct status when callers must tell them apart.
A state flag written without the mutex is a data race; make it _Atomic or touch it only while the mutex is held.
Every balk path after a successful trylock must unlock the mutex, or the object stays wedged for all later callers.
